summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey puts AI use in transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) at 13.0% of firms in the latest period, up from 7.9% in the prior period. The question asked is narrow: in the last two weeks, did this business use AI. The survey first asked about AI in September 2023, and the Census Bureau notes that some values are suppressed. That 13.0% is the only measured adoption figure in this material, and it describes firms answering yes to a two-week recall question, not the depth or sophistication of what they run.

What the sources show being deployed splits into two layers. The visible layer is autonomy: Aurora describes the Aurora Driver as self-driving freight technology backed by verifiable AI, integrated into fleets and into the Volvo VNL Autonomous, and Waymo publishes a safety program for fully autonomous driving, tracing its origin to the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009 and its first fully autonomous rides in 2015. The quieter layer is operational AI already in commercial use. Samsara describes a connected operations platform that analyzes the information it collects to produce AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights, alongside AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, drowsiness detection, and equipment management. C.H. Robinson frames its managed solutions as autonomous logistics orchestration, where the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes, and improves continuously across every shipment, and it runs an AI assistant on its own site. Wärtsilä lists AI-driven predictive analytics among the tools it uses for marine decarbonisation, and Airbus describes a decarbonised, connected and autonomous future for aerospace built on digitised operations.

Vendors and money concentrate where fleets and networks are large. Samsara says its platform helps 20,000+ operations improve safety, cut costs, and run smarter, and credits its safety technologies with 380,000+ accidents prevented. Aurora's page carries customer testimony about a pilot hauling freight autonomously between Fort Worth and El Paso and about a hybrid model pairing professional drivers with the Aurora Driver on long-haul routes. C.H. Robinson sells scale, experience, and data as the basis of supply chain management. The American Trucking Associations, which says it has more than 37,000 members, is the industry body in this material tracking policy and adoption for autonomous freight and AI logistics.

The ROI evidence the sources report is mostly safety and efficiency rather than financial return. Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented is the largest quantified claim here, tied to cameras, in-cab alerts, and coaching that reduce risky behaviors. Aurora's customers describe safety and efficiency benefits, better lives for drivers through handling lengthier and less desirable routes, and confidence from consistent performance over millions of autonomous miles. One Aurora customer states that freight volumes are projected to grow five fold between 2010-2050, making autonomous transport a necessity rather than an innovation. Waymo argues the status quo of road safety is unacceptable and that autonomous driving technology can save lives and improve mobility, and it aligns its work with the Vision Zero Network and the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy. None of these sources report a payback period, cost per mile, or margin figure.

The regulatory posture is gated and still forming. The International Maritime Organization adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, as voluntary guidance that complements existing maritime regulations, maintains technology neutrality, and is designed to facilitate a future transition into a mandatory instrument. The IMO states that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely controlled, though trials have shown larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out its vision for safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation and a comprehensive action plan for its AI Programme, amended once a year. This site's own sourced points describe the FAA's innovation work and EASA's AI roadmap as the regulatory record for AI flight systems, automated risk management, and eVTOL certification, with nothing flying commercially without them.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material suggests separating what is measured from what is marketed. The Census Bureau's 13.0% describes current, broad, shallow use across transportation and warehousing firms, while the autonomy programs from Aurora and Waymo, the maritime code from the IMO, and the aviation roadmap from EASA describe a frontier that is heavily gated by certification and rulemaking. The deployed, revenue-generating AI in these sources looks more like Samsara's telematics and predictive maintenance, C.H. Robinson's load and route prediction, and Wärtsilä's vessel analytics than like driverless corridors. This site's Robotics Models catalogue tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, including vision-language-action models, refreshed daily, which is where a reader can watch the underlying capability move.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The page catalogues the 1,000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each one's licence, download count and release date, and refreshing the set daily. It states that the catalogue is built from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page records that it was last verified on 2026-10-02.
